title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. Data: a base scheme R, an R-scheme S, and a fibred category F over (Sch)/R (for example quasi-coherent modules). A crystal of type F on S relative to R assigns an object of F to each infinitesimal thickening of S over R (the category C), with compatible transition isomorphisms. 'Valeur en S' is evaluation at S itself.

(i) Example 1 (crystals on a field k of characteristic p are p-adic systems over W) is a special case of Example 3 (S a closed subscheme of R; crystals are compatible systems on the infinitesimal neighbourhoods S_n, i.e. coherent modules on the formal completion of R along S). The reason is Cohen structure theory: any thickening of k lifts compatibly to W, so absolute crystals on k are the same as crystals on Spec k relative to Spec W, and Spec k is closed in Spec W.

(ii) Examples 2 (S étale over R) and 3 (S closed in R) have a common generalisation: S -> R unramified. An unramified morphism locally factors as a closed immersion into an étale R-scheme, so one can still form infinitesimal neighbourhoods S_n, and these are final in C.

(iii) Section 1.8 sets up stratifications in modern terms.
- Δ_n is the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in S x_R S, with projections p_1, p_2.
- An n-connection on E in F_S is an isomorphism p_1^*E ≅ p_2^*E on Δ_n restricting to the identity on Δ_0.
- A pseudo-stratification (∞-connection) is a compatible family of n-connections for all n.
- A stratification is a pseudo-stratification satisfying the cocycle condition on the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal of S x_R S x_R S. This is a formal descent datum along the formal completion of the diagonal, i.e. a module over the ring of differential operators in the sense of Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' and Berthelot.
- If Ω^1_{S/R} = 0, every Δ_n equals S. Then each object has a unique stratification, and stratified objects are just objects of F_S. The forgetful functor ('valeur en S') from stratified objects to F_S is always faithful.
- A crystal M yields M(S) with a canonical stratification: the two pullbacks of M(S) to Δ_n are both identified with M(Δ_n). This gives a functor from crystals to stratified objects. By remark 1.4 (W-modules -> tensor with k) it is not faithful in general. The next page states it is an equivalence for formally smooth S/R, and conjecturally for flat, locally finitely presented S/R.

Purpose: compare the crystal formalism with the differential (connection/stratification) formalism, the basis of the crystalline-de Rham comparison.
errors: Slip: under Ω^1_{S/R}=0 the category of stratified objects of F_S is equivalent to F_S itself, not to 'la catégorie F_R elle même'. This is confirmed by the next page ('équivalentes ... à F_S lui-même').

Implicit gap: Ω^1_{S/R}=0 forces Δ_n = Δ_0 only when the diagonal ideal I satisfies I/I^2 = 0 at every level, which holds since all I^k/I^{k+1} are quotients of tensor powers of I/I^2. So the claim is fine. The bridge 'Ω=0 implies the S_n are defined' for unramified morphisms needs locally-of-finite-type hypotheses (EGA IV 18.4), which are not stated.

Note on 1.4: in the Example-1 case (S=Spec k, R=Spec W, k perfect) stratified objects are just k-vector spaces. The non-faithfulness is that of tensoring with k over W, so the reference is consistent.

ideas.what: Absolute crystals on k equal crystals relative to W via Cohen; Example 1 is a special case of the closed-subscheme example
ideas.modern_name: Crystals on the infinitesimal site of a closed subscheme = modules on the formal completion
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Unramified S->R as common generalisation of the étale and closed-immersion cases, via infinitesimal neighbourhoods of unramified morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Infinitesimal neighbourhoods of unramified morphisms (EGA IV 16.4/18.4)

ideas.what: n-connections, pseudo-stratifications (∞-connections), stratifications as formal descent data along the completed diagonal
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés); EGA IV 16.8 for differential operators

ideas.what: Functor from crystals to stratified modules, not faithful in general
ideas.modern_name: Crystal -> stratified module comparison (Berthelot-Ogus 'Notes on crystalline cohomology', ch. 2)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes

deep.surprise_reason: Expository part of the well-known 1966 crystals letter. Everything here was developed in Grothendieck's IHES crystals notes and by Berthelot. The only notable item is the term 'pseudo-stratification' for a non-cocycle ∞-connection, which is minor terminology.
transcription_corrections: 'équivalente, par le foncteur "valeur en S", à la catégorie F_R elle même' is what is typed, but mathematically it should read F_S (author's slip, not a transcription error).
'[-deux-]' crossed out before 'exemples 2 et 3' is correct; 'On' corrects a typed 'Oa'.
'Une ∞-connexion' has a handwritten mark above/below 'Une'; the typed 'oo-connexion' is correctly read as ∞-connexion.
'sorites' (typed 'soriites' with correction) is correct; 'admet' corrects a typed 'addet'; 'seule' corrects 'seuke'.
